title: Estimated Average Glucose
description: Estimates mean plasma glucose from HbA1c using the ADAG formula validated by the American Diabetes Association.
purpose: Used to estimates mean plasma glucose from hba1c using the adag formula validated by the american diabetes association.

advice: Use eAG to translate HbA1c into a unit (mg/dL) that patients already understand from home glucose monitoring.
eAG represents the average glucose over the preceding 2–3 months.
The ADA recommends an HbA1c target of < 7% (eAG ≈ 154 mg/dL) for most non-pregnant adults with diabetes.
warnings: eAG may be inaccurate in conditions affecting red blood cell lifespan (e.g. iron deficiency anaemia, sickle cell trait, pregnancy).
This formula is derived from continuous glucose monitoring studies and may differ from self-monitored blood glucose averages.
Use as a guide only; individual glucose targets should be personalized.
followUp: If eAG is above target, review current diabetes management including diet, exercise, and medications.
Consider continuous glucose monitoring for more detailed glycemic assessment.
Recheck HbA1c in 3 months after therapy changes.

faq.question: What is estimated average glucose?
faq.answer: eAG converts your HbA1c into an average blood glucose value in mg/dL over the past 2–3 months, making it easier to compare with home glucose readings.

faq.question: What HbA1c equals an eAG of 126 mg/dL?
faq.answer: An eAG of 126 mg/dL corresponds to an HbA1c of approximately 6.0%.

faq.question: Is eAG the same as average blood glucose?
faq.answer: eAG is a statistical estimate of average glucose validated by CGM studies. It may not exactly match simple averages of finger-stick measurements.

evidence: Nathan DM, Steffes MW, et al. International multicenter A1c-derived average glucose (ADAG) study. Diabetes Care. 2008;31:1913–1917.
